title: Unclear ownership semantics for methods that return non-RefCounted objects.
body:
This was a topic discussed in the last GDExtension meeting, I was advised to open an issue by @dsnopek.  

Class methods that return non-RefCounted objects do not have clear ownership semantics. This is affecting both GDScript and GDExtension, such that when passing a non-RefCounted Object to a method, or when receiving a non-RefCounted Object from a method, it's not clear who is responsible for freeing the Object nor how long the Object needs to be kept alive for.

It entirely depends on the implementation of the method and whether or not any references to an Objects are kept by ID, or as pointers.

If an Object is freed inappropriately, at worst, this can result in undefined behavior, at best it can be a source of bugs.

In graphics.gd, I am maintaining a list of affected methods and determined ownership semantics which are designed to help the graphics.gd GDExtension interface layer improve memory-safety when working with non-RefCounted objects.

https://github.com/quaadgras/graphics.gd/blob/release/internal/gdjson/ownership.go

This structure maps classes to method names to argument names (or the "return value").

NOTE: the ownership semantics may not be accurate but could be of use to anyone affected by this issue.

### Steps to reproduce

Call a method that returns/accepts a non-RefCounted object and immediately free this object after calling the method, continue to observe for undefined behavior and/or crashes caused by this.
